title: Activate the killer heuristic in movetime searches
defect_found: self.killers is allocated only in search_with_params (alphabeta.rs:1597). search_movetime never allocated it, and the Default leaves it Vec::new(). Both killer_bonus and update_killers early-return when the ply index is past the end of that vector, so with length 0 they always did. Every movetime search therefore ran with the killer heuristic switched on (compare_play calls set_use_killers(true) at three sites) and doing nothing -- and movetime is the path compare_play, the model gate, and real games all take. The acceptance suite was unaffected because `accept` goes through search_with_params, which does allocate.
change_tested: PieBot/src/search/alphabeta_temp.rs search_movetime: allocate self.killers = vec![[None, None]; 256] alongside the other per-search state.

acceptance.note: identical to baseline, confirming the change is scoped to the movetime path and does not touch the fixed-depth suite

conclusion: Exactly 59-59-282: the mean pair delta is 0.0000 to four decimals. Killers add nothing measurable on top of the existing ordering (TT move first, MVV-LVA, SEE, butterfly history, counter-moves) at the depths reached in 150 ms. Not promoted -- the repo's criterion is a paired-bootstrap LCB above zero, and this arm has a symmetric CI centered on zero. The allocation was reverted; alphabeta_temp.rs is back to the re-export stub.
kept_separately: The five empty-bodied setters this investigation surfaced (set_null_min_depth, set_hist_min_depth, set_root_see_top_k, set_use_futility, set_use_lmp) were deleted along with their 13 call sites in compare_play.rs and bench.rs. That is a pure measurement-integrity fix with no behavioural change: the matein3 signature is unchanged at 14298048. Both harnesses had been configured differently than their operators believed -- bench.rs in particular was setting futility and LMP 'on' and null_min_depth to 8 when the real null-move floor is 3.
caveat: This result is measured against the post-S6 baseline. Killers may become worth re-testing if move ordering changes substantially -- for instance after continuation history lands, which would alter what the quiet-move ordering already captures.
